issues.detail: The Greek 'τι θελω' (ti thelo) means 'what I want' or 'what I wish', but the Vietnamese 'ước gì' (I wish/hope) combined with the passive construction 'đã được nhóm lên' (had been kindled) changes the sense of the subject's desire. The Greek implies a desire for the fire to be already burning/kindled, whereas the Vietnamese phrasing suggests a regretful wish about a past state.
